input: Track every meal for a full two weeks

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether to track only main meals or also snacks, drinks, and condiments changes how detailed and demanding the logging will be.
The underlying goal — losing weight, managing a health condition, understanding habits, or something else — determines which data points actually matter to capture.
Tracking for oneself is very different from tracking for a nutritionist, doctor, or coach who will review the data, which affects the required format and level of detail.
A hard time limit on how long each log entry can take shapes which tracking method is realistic to sustain for 14 days.
The tool chosen — a paper journal, a spreadsheet, or an app like MyFitnessPal — determines the immediate first action and how data is stored and reviewed.
Whether the user cares about calories, macros, ingredients, portion sizes, mood, or just meal names changes what fields need to be logged each time.
Knowing whether meals happen at home, at work, in restaurants, or across travel days affects how practical different tracking approaches will be.

gold.taskTitle: Track every meal for two full weeks
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to log all meals consistently across a 14-day period, but the method, purpose, and depth of tracking are all unclear.

questions.title: What counts as a loggable eating event for you?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants to track only main meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) or also snacks, beverages, sauces, and small bites throughout the day.

questions.title: What is the main reason you are doing this?
questions.description: Identify the underlying goal — weight loss, nutrition awareness, medical monitoring, building a habit, or something else — so the most relevant data points are prioritised.

questions.title: Will anyone else review your meal logs?
questions.description: Determine whether a nutritionist, doctor, coach, or accountability partner will see the data, which affects how formal and detailed the entries need to be.

questions.title: How much time per entry can you realistically spend?
questions.description: Establish a per-log time budget so the chosen method stays sustainable across the full two weeks without becoming a burden.

questions.title: Which tool do you want to use for logging?
questions.description: Decide between a phone app, a spreadsheet, a paper journal, or another format, as this determines the immediate first action and how data is stored.

questions.title: Which details matter most to capture each meal?
questions.description: Find out whether the user needs calories, macros, portion sizes, ingredients, hunger levels, mood, or just the name of what was eaten.

questions.title: Where will most of your meals take place?
questions.description: Understand whether meals are mostly home-cooked, eaten at the office, ordered from restaurants, or spread across travel, as this shapes which tracking approach is practical.
